title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 331 (Liabilities and rights of certain persons fraudulently preferred)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up and a fraudulent preference has been given, any person who is preferred and who was a creditor at the time is subject to the same liabilities and has the same rights as if he had undertaken to be personally liable as surety for the debt to the extent of the preference; the section also regulates recovery and contribution among persons liable.
content.glance: A fraudulently preferred person is treated as a surety to the extent of the preference; recovery and contribution rules apply.
content.study: Section 331 attaches consequences to a person who has received a fraudulent preference. That person is put in the position of a surety for the preferred debt to the extent of the preference and becomes subject to corresponding liabilities and rights. The provision facilitates recovery for the estate and apportions responsibility among those who benefited. Sub-provisions address the measure of liability and contribution among co-liable persons, applying mutatis mutandis to non-money transactions.

sections.heading: Surety-like liability of preferred person
sections.body: A fraudulently preferred creditor is treated as having undertaken personal liability as surety for the debt to the extent of the preference.

sections.heading: Recovery and contribution
sections.body: The estate may recover; contribution rules apply among persons liable, including for non-money transactions.

provisions.title: Liabilities and rights of certain persons fraudulently preferred

examples.title: Preferred creditor as surety
examples.body: A creditor who received a fraudulent preference repayment is treated under s. 331 as a surety to the extent of that preference and may be required to restore value for the benefit of the estate.

hypotheticals.question: What is the measure of liability of a fraudulently preferred person?
hypotheticals.analysis: The person is treated as a surety for the debt to the extent of the preference; recovery and contribution follow the statutory rules.

rows.left: Consequences for the preferred person (surety liability)
rows.right: Tribunal power to set aside the preference

misconceptions.trap: Only the company is liable after a fraudulent preference is set aside.
misconceptions.correction: The preferred person is placed in a surety-like position to the extent of the preference and may be required to restore value.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 331 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm fraudulent preference under s. 328. II. Apply the surety-like liability and recovery/contribution rules of s. 331.

examTips: Link s. 331 consequences to a finding of fraudulent preference under s. 328.
revisionPoints: Preferred person treated as surety to extent of preference
